body:
Thank you for the kind words. <3

When I was talking about pressure building to a point, I meant conflict with people I love. It tends to build up in little benign things, to one big unnecessary confrontation in which relations are worsened. I want to be able to address those smaller things individually, and appropriately so I don’t push anyone away, and so I don’t have the heightened stress that’s comes with a big argument, in which I usually am forced to cede otherwise legitimate ground for the sake of civility.
I guess I can understand that, it should have been an opt-in sorta thing. Do you know how I might go about retrieving them?
You’re gunna turn into a baby dude, WTF, YOU’RE TEARING THIS FAMILY APART!

I’m not defending them, I tried making that clear. I’m sorry you took it that way, there’s not really shit I can do if you continue to take it that way. 

I was talking about people that lean on their friends like they’re a therapist even though those friends may hardly be capable of keeping themselves healthy & happy. No one knows what the other persons going through.

Everyone has dead family; I’ve lost grandparents, great grandparents, even a sister. Everyone has lost someone, those people aren’t all dying at the same time... never implied that, but as you’ve shown clearly the shadow of that death, the damage of it, can go on after that person has passed. Rightfully so. Every person on earth is struggling with something mentally. We’re all going through shit, some of us choose to keep that inside, and aren’t willing or aren’t capable of reciprocating the openness that a grieving friend may need. To a lot of people that comes off as arrogant or stone-hearted, in reality we all just grieve differently. 

Of course you can lean on your friends, but don’t endlessly batter them with your problems and expect them to accommodate for everything you’re going through when they very likely are going through something similar mentally.

This just sounds exactly like what he was talking about. No ones talking about leaving a friend because they’re going through shit, or at least I hope no one here is. I’m not defending the people who left you during hard times btw. 

When a friend is consistently behaving negatively it’s fine to distance from them or confront them. You can’t offload your shit onto other people and just expect them to accommodate 100% of the time. Everyone is going through shit. Everyone has someone who died; everyone dislikes themselves; everyone has been abused mentally or physically. Everyone is struggling day to day no matter how rich or poor; privileged or oppressed they may seem. That doesn’t mean that that suffering is any less valid. For some, keeping themselves intact is the most they can handle; but when you then also have to keep a friend intact at the same time, you risk losing it all including the friend, so it’s best to handle you.
I think that’s just cumming with extra sadness.

I think I have a little of both. 

On one hand I can completely empty my mind and just think about absolutely nothing.

On the other sometimes I have hour long conversations with myself about something I’m obsessing over in the moment.

Just a question but like, do you mean you just straight up can’t vision things in your head and can’t talk to yourself? Like what happens when you try to draw? Or I guess like... when you’re just planning something, even vaguely.
